title: High Winds, Rain, Ice & Fog
whatItIs: High-sided vehicles are the most affected by strong winds. In rain, ice and fog, slow down, leave much bigger gaps and use your lights when visibility is seriously reduced.
keyFacts: High-sided vehicles are most affected by wind, especially on exposed roads and when passing bridges or gaps in hedges.
In very windy weather, turbulence from large vehicles can affect others. Motorcyclists are particularly affected.
Give cyclists, motorcyclists, horse riders and pedestrians more space when overtaking in high winds.

keyFacts.text: You MUST use headlights when visibility is seriously reduced, generally below 100 metres.
You MUST NOT use fog lights unless visibility is seriously reduced, and MUST switch them off when it improves.

keyFacts: On ice, drive slowly in as high a gear as possible. Accelerate and brake very gently.

items.title: Strong wind
items.text: Expect gusts on exposed roads, at bridges and at gaps in hedges.

items.title: Rain
items.text: Stopping distances at least double. Steering unresponsive? Ease off and slow down gradually.

items.title: Ice and snow
items.text: Stopping distances up to ten times greater. Clear all windows before you set off.

items.title: Fog
items.text: Headlights if you cannot see beyond 100 m. Be able to stop within the distance you can see.

a.label: Headlights
points: MUST be used when visibility is seriously reduced
Generally when you cannot see for more than 100 metres

b.label: Fog lights
points: Only when visibility is seriously reduced
MUST be switched off when visibility improves

onTheTest.question: You're driving a high-sided lorry in strong winds. Where are you most likely to meet a sudden gust?
options: Passing a gap in a hedge
Waiting at traffic lights in town
Following a car at a safe distance
onTheTest.why: High-sided vehicles are most affected by wind. Strong gusts happen on exposed open roads, or when passing bridges or gaps in hedges.

onTheTest.question: When must you use headlights in poor weather?
options: When visibility is seriously reduced, generally under 100 metres
onTheTest.why: You must use headlights when visibility is seriously reduced, generally when you cannot see for more than 100 metres.

traps: Wind doesn't only affect you: your lorry's turbulence can push motorcyclists off course.
Fog lights left on after the fog clears dazzle others and can hide your brake lights.
On ice, tyres make virtually no noise: quiet tyres and unresponsive steering are warning signs.
